Create a ScreenR object

Source: R/create_object.R
create_screenr_object.Rd

Creates the ScreenR object, the starting point of every analysis, from a count table and an annotation table. The object stores the counts, the annotation, the groups of the samples and, later, the normalized counts and the data table.

Usage

create_screenr_object(
  table = NULL,
  annotation = NULL,
  groups = NULL,
  replicates = c(""),
  barcode_column = "Barcode",
  gene_column = "Gene",
  sample_table = NULL,
  sample_columns = c(Sample = "Sample", Day = "Day", Treatment = "Treatment")
)

Arguments

table

The count table obtained from the read alignment, with one row for each barcode and one column for each sample, plus the barcode column.

annotation

The annotation table, with one row for each barcode and at least the barcode column and the gene column (the gene targeted by the shRNA).

groups

A factor with the experimental group of each sample (for example "Control" and "Treated"), with one value for each sample (column of the count table other than the barcode column). It is used by the edgeR/limma based methods, see create_design_matrix.

replicates

An optional vector with the replicate labels. Default c("").

barcode_column

The name of the column containing the barcode identifiers, in both the count and the annotation table. Default "Barcode".

gene_column

The name of the column of the annotation table containing the gene names. Default "Gene".

sample_table

An optional data frame with one row for each sample and columns giving the sample name, the Day (time point) and the Treatment of the sample. When given, these values are used instead of the ones derived from the sample names.

sample_columns

A named character vector giving the names of the columns of sample_table that contain the sample names, the Day and the Treatment. Default c(Sample = "Sample", Day = "Day", Treatment = "Treatment").

Value

A ScreenR object (class screenr_object).

Details

The tables can use any column names: the names of the barcode and gene columns are given with barcode_column and gene_column, and the object renames them internally to Barcode and Gene (the original names are kept, see get_column_names). When a column is not found, the error suggests the most similar column name.

The input is checked when the object is created:

  • sample columns stored as text but containing only numbers are converted to numbers;

  • other non-numeric columns of the count table (for example a gene column) are removed with a message, since they are not samples;

  • groups must have one value for each sample;

  • barcodes that are duplicated, or that are missing from the annotation (for example the unmapped reads "*"), give a warning.

The Day (time point) and the Treatment of each sample are used by several functions. By default they are taken from the sample names, which must have the form Day_Treatment_Replicate (for example Time3_TRT_A). When the sample names have another form, give them explicitly with sample_table, and check the result with get_sample_table.

See also

normalize_data, compute_data_table, get_sample_table, get_count_table and the other accessors.

Examples

count_table <-
    data.frame(
        Barcode = c("Code_1", "Code_2", "Code_3", "Code_4"),
        Time3_CTRL_rep1 = c(3520, 3020, 1507, 1400),
        Time3_CTRL_rep2 = c(3500, 3000, 1457, 1490),
        Time3_TRT_rep1 = c(1200, 1100, 1300, 1350),
        Time3_TRT_rep2 = c(1250, 1000, 1400, 1375)
    )
annotation_table <-
    data.frame(
        Gene = c("Gene_1", "Gene_1", "Gene_2", "Gene_2"),
        Barcode = c("Code_1", "Code_2", "Code_3", "Code_4")
    )

groups <- factor(c("Control", "Control", "Treated", "Treated"))
obj <- create_screenr_object(
    table = count_table,
    annotation = annotation_table,
    groups = groups, replicates = c("")
)
obj
#> class: screenr_object 
#> dim: 4 4 
#> metadata(0):
#> assays(1): counts
#> rownames(4): Code_1 Code_2 Code_3 Code_4
#> rowData names(2): Barcode Gene
#> colnames(4): Time3_CTRL_rep1 Time3_CTRL_rep2 Time3_TRT_rep1
#>   Time3_TRT_rep2
#> colData names(4): Sample Day Treatment Group
#> data table: 0 rows, 0 columns

# Tables with other column names and sample names without the
# Day_Treatment_Replicate form
counts <- count_table
colnames(counts) <- c("shRNA", "c1", "c2", "t1", "t2")
annotation <- data.frame(
    symbol = annotation_table$Gene,
    shRNA = annotation_table$Barcode
)
samples <- data.frame(
    id = c("c1", "c2", "t1", "t2"),
    time = "Day3",
    condition = c("CTRL", "CTRL", "TRT", "TRT")
)
obj <- create_screenr_object(
    table = counts, annotation = annotation, groups = groups,
    barcode_column = "shRNA", gene_column = "symbol",
    sample_table = samples,
    sample_columns = c(Sample = "id", Day = "time",
        Treatment = "condition")
)
get_sample_table(obj)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 3
#>   Sample Day   Treatment
#>   <chr>  <chr> <chr>    
#> 1 c1     Day3  CTRL     
#> 2 c2     Day3  CTRL     
#> 3 t1     Day3  TRT      
#> 4 t2     Day3  TRT      
get_column_names(obj)
#>     Barcode        Gene      Sample         Day   Treatment 
#>     "shRNA"    "symbol"        "id"      "time" "condition"
